name: Klettersteig Kandersteg–Allmenalp
approach: 10 min from the Allmenalp cable-car valley station car park
lift: Allmenalp cable car (Kandersteg ↔ Allmenalp) — used for the descent, not needed for the approach
descent: 20 min on foot to the Allmenalp top station; walking all the way down to Kandersteg takes about 1 h 15
character: Waterfalls, Nepalese bridges, several ladder pitches and a Tyrolienne. The crux is an overhanging traverse below the three-cable bridge.
caveat: Very popular — go early. The route finishes at the top station, so you can ride down or walk.

name: Chäligang-Klettersteig
approach: 20 min from the car park at the Engstligenalp cable-car valley station
lift: Engstligenalp cable car — optional; the ferrata starts from the valley
descent: 1 h on foot back down to the car park
character: Short, generously protected beginner route running right beside the Engstligen falls, with a rest platform overlooking the cascade.
caveat: Ideal first via ferrata. Wide paths, little exposure.
imgCredit: No machine-readable author provided. Irmgard assumed (based on copyright claims) · CC BY-SA 3.0

name: Gantrisch-Klettersteig
approach: 45 min from the Nünenenberg car park
descent: 1 h 30 via the Leiterenpass back to the car park
character: Demanding route with overhangs and deliberately offset iron rungs. The lower Küre-Wändli and the airy Horber-Kante near the top are the key sections.
caveat: No lift anywhere — entirely a walking day. Rock can be brittle in places.

name: Klettersteig Sunnighorn (Simmeflue)
approach: 20 min from the Schnitzelscheune (Brodhüsi) car park in Wimmis
character: A hiking day with beginner ferrata sections spliced in, climbing steeply above Lake Thun. Aimed squarely at people trying via ferrata for the first time.
caveat: Dry conditions only — the descent gets slippery. Big vertical gain for a K2.

name: Übungsklettersteig Hornflue
approach: Short walk from the Hornberg; reachable by road or by lift from Saanenmöser
character: A tiny practice ferrata — two short lines on the Hornflue with big views over the whole Saanenland.
caveat: Really a training wall rather than a day out. Good for testing gear or technique.

name: Klettersteig Mürren–Gimmelwald
approach: 15 min from Mürren village
lift: Schilthornbahn (Stechelberg–Gimmelwald–Mürren) to reach Mürren; Gimmelwald cable car at the finish
descent: The route itself descends to Gimmelwald; from there the cable car (or a walk) down to Stechelberg
character: A descending ferrata traversing the cliffs above Lauterbrunnen with roughly 600 m of air underfoot, finishing on an 80 m Nepalese bridge.
caveat: Point-to-point and downhill — plan the transport. Earthy, root-covered ledges get slippery when wet.

name: Eiger-Rotstock-Klettersteig
approach: 45 min from Eigergletscher station
descent: 45 min from the Rotstock back to Eigergletscher
character: Alpine route on the Rotstock with the Eiger north face as a backdrop. An 1899 iron ladder and steps chiselled into the limestone give it real historical character.
caveat: Loose rock in places; the descent over slabs is adventurous despite the easy grade.

name: Klettersteig Eiger-Ostegghütte
ferrataTime: ~3 h total from Alpiglen to the hut
approach: 45 min from Alpiglen station along the Eiger Trail to the junction
lift: Grindelwald–Alpiglen train (or walk up from Grindelwald)
character: A hut approach rather than a summit route — a secured line up a gorge with three steep steps, ending at the Ostegghütte on its grass balcony high above Grindelwald.
caveat: One smooth slab is the crux and much harder than the rest. Needs sure footing and a genuinely good head for heights.

name: Schwarzhorn-Klettersteig
approach: 2 h from the First cable-car top station
character: Long walk-in, then moderately difficult climbing on very airy offset ladders to a 2928 m summit. About 920 m of total height difference over the day.
caveat: High and committing — needs settled weather. Roughly 5 h round trip from First.

name: Tälli-Klettersteig
approach: 1 h from the Tälli cable-car top station (1726 m)
descent: 2 h 30, including a counter-ascent to the Sätteli
character: Switzerland's first modern via ferrata (1993). A 630 m south-facing wall of ladders and traversing bands with genuine alpine flair.
caveat: The descent is long and involves re-ascending — a full 6½ h day. Old snow can linger at the entry in early summer.

name: Tierbergli-Klettersteig
approach: 5 min from the Umpol car park at the end of the road past the Steingletscher
lift: None — road access over the Susten pass
descent: 2 h on the blue-white alpine trail
character: High alpine ferrata with glacier views and a lot of real rock contact — slabs first, then steeper ground with scree and snow patches marked by red dots.
caveat: Short season. Snowfields on the upper section; the pass road is closed in winter.

name: Klettersteig Eggishorn
approach: 15 min from the Eggishorn top station
descent: Back down by cable car from Eggishorn station
character: Traverses blocky ground along the Fiescherhorli ridge with a suspension bridge, a three-cable bridge, a timber bridge and an optional zip-line — all above the Great Aletsch Glacier.
caveat: Mid-route exit available after about an hour. Very exposed to weather at 2800 m.

name: Klettersteig Aletsch (Gibidum)
ferrataTime: ~2 h per bank, ~4 h for the full circuit
approach: Short walk from the car park at the Gibidum reservoir dam
character: About 3 km of ferrata circling the Gibidum reservoir, crossing an impressive suspension bridge and a cable crossing, alternating forest with exposed rock right above the water.
caveat: The eastern return leg is the harder half, with iron rungs spaced further apart. Low altitude — good early- and late-season option.

name: Erlebnisklettersteig Gemmiwand
approach: 2–5 min from the Gemmibahn top station
descent: Back to the top station; or walk down the historic Gemmi trail to Leukerbad
descentFoot: ~1 h 30 down the Gemmiweg to Leukerbad
character: A French-style sports ferrata running roughly horizontally for about 1300 m across the Gemmi wall below the Wildstrubel restaurant. Highlights are a 65 m rope bridge and a ladder that rotates through 540°.
caveat: Almost no height gain but sustained and very exposed — arm strength matters more than fitness.

name: Leukerbadner Klettersteig (Daubenhorn)
approach: ~30 min from the Gemmibahn top station
approachFoot: +1 h and 650 m extra if you walk up from Leukerbad
lift: Gemmibahn (optional — the route can be done entirely on foot)
descent: From the summit down to the Gemmi pass and back to the station, ~2 h
descentFoot: ~2 h 30 further down the Gemmi trail to Leukerbad
character: The longest and hardest via ferrata in Switzerland: 1100 m of gain, 216 m of ladders and over 2000 m of steel cable, including a ~100 m natural cave passage.
caveat: A serious full day. An escape route exists roughly a third of the way up; after that you are committed.

name: Baltschieder Klettersteig (Wiwannihütte)
approach: ~2 h from Ausserberg station through the Baltschiedertal along the historic Niwärch suone
character: The finest and hardest way up to the Wiwannihütte: steep rock, grass ledges and a striking rock tower. Around 5 h for the ascent, 8 h for the whole day.
caveat: Remote and long. The Niwärch suone approach is itself exposed. No lift, no shortcuts.

name: Via Farinetta
approach: 30 min from the car park at the Bains de Saillon thermal baths
character: Three stacked sections of increasing severity, with cable bridges at the start, a rope-liana passage and a strenuous overhanging final wall. Exits after each section.
caveat: Low, south-facing and hot in summer — best in spring or autumn. Section 3 at K6 is for strong climbers only.

name: Via ferrata de Tière
approach: 30 min from the main car park in Champéry village centre
descent: 1 h, via the impressive Galerie Defago
character: Varied sports ferrata with two suspension bridges at a waterfall; vertical steps alternating with exposed traverses. The crux is slightly overhanging.
caveat: Wet rock near the falls. Low altitude makes it a good shoulder-season option.

name: Via ferrata Tour d'Aï
approach: 45 min from the Berneuse top station
character: Airy limestone route to a proper summit with sweeping views over Lake Geneva and across to the Valais Alps.
caveat: Iron rungs are widely spaced in the couloir section — awkward for shorter climbers.

name: Via ferrata de la Tête aux Chamois
approach: You climb down to the start from the lift; ~15 min
lift: Glacier 3000 cable car from Col du Pillon
descent: Climb back up to the cable car at the finish, ~30 min
descentFoot: long — the lift is effectively required
character: French-style sports ferrata across the north side of the Tête aux Chamois: a chain of natural ledges that narrow to a single foot-width, plus the notorious Rocher Jaune traverse.
caveat: Technically moderate but ferociously exposed, with strength-sapping overhangs. Escape onto the scree a third of the way along.

name: Via ferrata de la Cascade du Dar
approach: 15 min from the Glacier 3000 valley station car park at Col du Pillon
character: French-style sports route: an overhanging traverse out to the waterfall, a demanding cable bridge at the very start and a narrow squeeze near the cascade.
caveat: Slippery in the spray zone. Very little height gain but sustained on the arms.

name: Via ferrata de Pierredar (Dames Anglaises)
approach: 45 min–1 h from the Refuge de Pierredar; about 4 h on foot from Les Diablerets
character: 430 m of route high above the Pierredar refuge, replacing the older Pierredar line that was destroyed by rockfall.
caveat: Long, remote approach — realistically an overnight at the refuge. Officially K2 but with distinctly harder passages.

name: Via ferrata de Plan Praz
approach: 20 min from Feydey in Leysin (1398 m)
character: Almost no height gain and entirely about difficulty: powerful overhangs, several suspension bridges, beams and ladders on a compact wall right above the village.
caveat: For strong, experienced climbers only. Two exit options.

name: Via ferrata du Lavanchy
approach: 1 h from the Pont-de-Nant car park
character: A very short, well-protected sports ferrata in a beautiful setting at the head of the Vallon de Nant, with mild overhangs and traverses.
caveat: Short — worth combining with the walk up to the Pont-de-Nant botanical garden. Not a beginner route despite its brevity.
peak: Pont de Nant Vallon de Nant

name: Via ferrata de la Videmanette (3 routes)
grade: Route 1 easy · Route 2 moderate · Route 3 very difficult
approach: 5 min from the La Videmanette top station
descent: Back to the top station, ~20 min
character: Three parallel routes of increasing difficulty (500 m / 380 m / 400 m) up to the summit of the Rubli, with a 360° panorama at the top.
caveat: The three grades make it an unusually good place to bring a mixed-ability group.

name: Via ferrata des Rochers de Naye
approach: ~20 min from Jaman station
descent: ~45 min back, or take the train down from Rochers-de-Naye
descentFoot: long — the railway is the sensible option
character: Steep, famously exposed limestone with the drop running straight down to Lake Geneva.
caveat: Has an escape route. Serious grade — not a first ferrata.

name: Via ferrata Le Moléson (Le Pilier – La Face)
approach: 10 min from the Plan-Francey middle station
lift: Moléson funicular to Plan-Francey, then cable car from the summit
descent: 2 h 30 on foot back to the car park, or ride the cable car down from the summit
character: Well-equipped sports route with abundant iron rungs and little direct rock contact. Two variants (left is easier), finishing on an exposed overhanging traverse.
caveat: North-facing, so cold in the morning. There is a voluntary maintenance donation box — access itself is free.

name: Via ferrata de Charmey
approach: 30 min from the Charmey cable-car top station
character: Cable nets, wire bridges, a cave and a Tibetan bridge, with three lines side by side. Summit views to the Gastlosen and the Moléson.
caveat: No intermediate exits — once you start you finish. Pick your line before committing.

name: Klettersteig Fürenwand
approach: 20 min from the Fürenalp cable-car valley station car park
lift: Fürenalp cable car — used for the descent
descent: By cable car from Fürenalp; walking down takes about 1 h 30
character: One of the undisputed Swiss classics: a sheer wall opposite the Titlis, with a steep exposed first section and a very airy 20 m rope ladder near the top.
caveat: Not for beginners. The rope ladder needs arm strength and nerve — there is no way round it.

name: Klettersteig Brunnistöckli
ferrataTime: 1 h from the cable-car station to the top
approach: From the Brunni cable-car top station
character: The classic Swiss beginner ferrata — short approach, about 200 m of gain and two suspension bridges. Popular with families.
caveat: Not recommended for children under 8. Gear rental at the lift (CHF 25).

name: Klettersteig Zittergrat
approach: From the Brunni cable-car top station
character: Right next to the Brunnistöckli and finishing at the same point, but short, steep and genuinely exposed — the hardest of the Brunni routes.
caveat: Needs arm strength and a good head. Often combined with the Brunnistöckli in one outing.

name: Klettersteig Rigidalstockgrat
approach: Long walk-in from the Brunni top station via the Brunni-Pfad
descent: 1 h 30 from Schonegg back to the Brunnihütte
character: The easier of the two Rigidalstock lines and suitable for beginners, but with a serious alpine walk-in and a proper 2577 m summit.
caveat: A full day. Often linked with the Brunnistöckli lower down.

name: Klettersteig Rigidalstockwand
approach: Same walk-in as the Grat route, from the Brunni top station
character: The wall variant on the Rigidalstock — steeper and harder than the ridge line, and explicitly not a beginner route.
caveat: Long day with a demanding finish. Check conditions at the Brunni lift.

name: Graustock-Klettersteig
approach: 1 h 10 from Engstlenalp to the Jochpass, plus 20 min; or start at the Jochpass lift station
character: Mixed mountain path over slabs linked by steep, exposed ferrata pitches. The crux is short and fierce, and you have to find your own holds.
caveat: The second part jumps to K4–K5 — check you are happy before committing past part 1.

name: Fruttlisteig (Bonistock)
approach: 30 min from Melchsee-Frutt
character: A tiny route through a rock band up towards the Bonistock. Its signature is an old chairlift seat bolted to the wall as a viewing perch over the Melchsee.
caveat: Very short — best treated as an add-on to a hiking day at Melchsee-Frutt.

name: Klettersteig Fruttstägä
approach: 1 h from the Biel-Kinzig cable-car top station
lift: Biel-Kinzig cable car from Brügg near Bürglen
descent: ~2 h back to the cable-car station
character: Short, well-protected route with an exposed sitting bench bolted to a near-vertical wall and a 10 m rope bridge near the finish.
caveat: The crux is right above the entry and slightly overhanging — there is an easier alternative line.

name: Klettersteig Klewenalp–Ergglen
approach: 30 min from the Klewenalp top station to the Ergglen barbecue site
descent: 30 min back to the top station
character: A short family route with three wire bridges and a cave-like passage, very well secured with plenty of iron steps, looking out over Lake Lucerne.
caveat: Genuinely tiny — a fun stop rather than a day, ideal for first-timers and children.

name: Klettersteig Adlerhorst
approach: 20 min from the Berggasthaus Alpenblick at Arnisee
descent: 45 min back to the cable-car station
season: Early May to end of November
character: Beginner-friendly, solidly protected route in lovely spruce forest surroundings: a short entry ladder, a leftward traverse and a small overhang as the crux.
caveat: Has an intermediate exit. Long season thanks to the modest altitude.

name: Via ferrata del Diavolo
approach: 15 min from the car park after the roundabout at the entrance to Andermatt
character: Exceptionally well-secured granite route above the Schöllenen gorge, with views down onto the Devil's Bridge and the road's hairpins.
caveat: The difficulty is the sheer length rather than any single move; a small overhang near the end is the crux. Gets busy.

name: Hexensteig am Pfaffen
approach: 1 h from the Chilcherberge cable-car top station
lift: Open-air Chilcherberge cable car (very limited parking at the valley station)
descentFoot: long — the little cable car is the practical option
character: Runs largely through the inside of the mountain, over tree trunks and iron steps, and opens with a Tyrolean traverse across a small gorge.
caveat: Steep, partly overhanging and dangerous when wet. The tiny open-air cable car has very limited capacity and parking.

name: Klettersteig Krokodil (Bergsee)
approach: 1 h from the Berggasthaus Dammagletscher car park to the Bergseehütte, then 20 min
descent: 20 min to the hut, then ~1 h back to the car park
season: While the Bergseehütte is staffed — contact the hut
character: 400 m of steel cable over two rock towers, the second of which really does look like a crocodile's head. Lots of direct rock contact and a wire bridge near the finish.
caveat: Views over the Bergsee, Göscheneralpsee and Dammagletscher. Best combined with a night at the Bergseehütte.

name: Klettersteig Schijen Zwärg
approach: On the T3 path from the Göscheneralpsee up to the Bergseehütte
descent: Continue to the Bergseehütte, then ~1 h back down
season: Summer, while the hut is staffed
character: A short, scenic ferrata spliced into the walk up to the Bergseehütte — a neat warm-up for the Krokodil route above.
caveat: Very short; only worth it as part of the Bergseehütte day.

name: Salbit-Höhenweg / Salbit-Kettenweg
approach: From the Ulmi car park (1195 m) or the Voralpkehre (1404 m); ~2 h 20 up to the Salbithütte
character: Not a pure ferrata: a long alpine day mixing hiking, scree and boulders with a 50 m secured wall, plus the spectacular 90 m Salbit suspension bridge on the Höhenweg to the Voralphütte.
caveat: About 1285 m of total gain and 7 h 30. The Salbithütte at 2105 m breaks it up.

name: Klettersteig Husky-Lodge & Felspfad
approach: 10 min from the car park at the Erlebniswelt Muotathal
character: Two well-protected lines side by side. The Felspfad is about as gentle an introduction to via ferrata as exists; the main route goes vertically up the wall, then a ladder, a ledge traverse and a final push.
caveat: Genuinely usable in winter, which is rare. Perfect for a first try or an off-season fix.
imgCredit: Earth Science and Remote Sensing Unit, Lyndon B. Johnson Space Center · Public domain

name: Rigi-Kulm-Nordwestrippe (Bänderweg)
approach: 30 min from Seebodenalp (1020 m), reached by a narrow road up from Küssnacht am Rigi; parking CHF 8 / 24 h
lift: None needed — road to Seebodenalp (a cable car from Küssnacht also serves it)
descent: 1 h 15 back down to Seebodenalp, or continue to Rigi Kulm and take the cog railway
character: The Bänderweg up the Rigi's north-west rib — three short rock steps and flower-covered ledges to the summit, well away from the cog-railway crowds. The key pitch is a steep 40 m nagelfluh band rigged with a 'pearl chain': steel cable threaded with plastic balls every 10 cm.
caveat: Not really a via ferrata. There is no continuous cable to clip into and a set is not needed — the pearl chain actively makes clipping awkward. Graded T5− as an alpine walk. Practically unwaymarked, and the steep grass is dangerous when wet.

name: Klettersteig Zingelstöckli
approach: 30 min on the path behind the former Gasthaus Tell in Urnerboden
season: Summer — the Klausen pass is closed in winter
character: Opened in 2016 on Switzerland's largest alp. A sporty line with steep and overhanging passages.
caveat: Strongly advised against in the wet. Not for beginners. Free parking by the church; gear can be hired in the village shop.

name: Braunwalder Klettersteig (Eggstöcke)
approach: ~50 min from the Berggasthaus Gumen (1904 m)
lift: Linthal–Braunwald funicular (Braunwald is car-free), then the Gumen chairlift
character: A ridge traverse over four summits of the Eggstöcke with escalating difficulty. The K5 section to the rear summit is overhanging with widely spaced holds; two intermediate exits allow a shorter day.
caveat: Beginner and children's variants exist near the mountain restaurant. Braunwald is car-free — factor the funicular into your timing.

name: Indianer-Klettersteig Netstal
approach: 30 min from the car park near the Schlattstein erratic beside the Linth in Netstal
season: Early season — usable when higher routes are still snowed in
character: Short but varied: a cave, a ladder and a Tyrolean traverse with a fixed pulley, finishing on an overhanging push to the top.
caveat: Exposed and technically demanding despite the low altitude. There is an emergency exit partway.

name: Speer-Kletterweg
ferrataTime: ~4–5 h to the summit in total
approach: 1 h 30 from the free Mittelwengi car park (1150 m) via the Obere Rossalpe
descent: 2 h 30; adding the Bützli descent variant costs about another 2 h 30
character: A secured climbing path up Europe's highest grass-covered peak, above the Walensee.
caveat: Closer to an exposed alpine route with cables than a modern sports ferrata. Long day.

name: Lisengrat & Nasenlöcherweg
approach: Via Schwägalp or Wasserauen; the Lisengrat links the Rotsteinpass to the Säntis summit
approachFoot: ~3 h from Wasserauen to the Rotsteinpass
lift: Säntis-Schwebebahn from Schwägalp; Ebenalp cable car from Wasserauen
descent: Säntis cable car, or walk down to Schwägalp
character: The famous exposed ridge from the Rotsteinpass to the Säntis, cable-protected throughout, plus the Nasenlöcherweg in the Alpstein.
caveat: A secured alpine path rather than a true via ferrata — most walkers do it without a ferrata set, but it is seriously exposed and dangerous in snow or ice.

name: Fläscher Leiterliweg
approach: Short walk from Fläsch above the Bündner Herrschaft vineyards
season: Almost all year — very low and sunny
character: A mini ferrata of ladders on the cliffs above Fläsch, with only 10–15 minutes of actual climbing.
caveat: Trivially short. Worth it as a warm-up combined with a walk in the Bündner Herrschaft.

name: Klettersteig Pinut
approach: 30 min up through the forest from Fidaz (200 m of gain); about 1 h 15 from Flims village
descent: 1 h 15 down to Bargis, then about 2 h back to Fidaz/Flims
character: First documented in 1739 and fully renovated in 2007 — the oldest via ferrata in Switzerland. Ladders and stairs through three rock faces and caves in the Flimserstein, separated by the Pinut and Pardatsch meadows.
caveat: Around 5 h for the whole tour. Easy technically but a long day; free access with a donation box.
imgCredit: upload by Adrian Michael · CC BY-SA 3.0

name: Sulzfluh-Klettersteig
approach: 1 h 30 from the car parks at the head of the Partnun valley (1700 m), on the marked path towards the Carschinahütte
character: The classic of the three Partnun routes: an exemplary south-facing line up brilliant white limestone with abundant rungs, short ladders, a cable bridge and a ladder bridge. 500–600 m of steel cable, and a famous rest ledge — the Bankli — halfway.
caveat: 1150 m of total gain and 6 h 30 for the day. The cable is removed for the winter.

name: Partnunblick-Klettersteig
approach: 2 h from car park no. 6 at Partnun (1631 m)
character: Climbs the Gemstobelwand with steadily rising difficulty, usually entered via the family route below. The short final wall is D/E and extremely exposed.
caveat: No emergency exit anywhere, and the crux waits until the very end. Experienced parties only.

name: Familien-Klettersteig Partnunblick
approach: 1 h 30 from car park no. 6 at Partnun (1631 m)
character: About 180 m zig-zagging up the wall with two short cable bridges and two platform pillars to exit from, high above the turquoise Partnunsee.
caveat: Recommended from age 8. 4 h 45 for the round trip — the walking, not the climbing, is the effort.

name: Gauablickhöhle-Klettersteig
approach: ~3 h, on the north side of the Sulzfluh
character: A moderate route on the north flank of the Sulzfluh whose highlight is entering the Gauablickhöhle — a 350 m cave — right in the middle of the climb.
caveat: Long approach and descent make this a big day. Take a head torch for the cave.

name: Klettersteig Punteglias
approach: Long walk-in up the Val Punteglias towards the Camona da Punteglias
character: A remote granite route in the Val Punteglias above Trun, usually combined with a visit to the Camona da Punteglias. Outdooractive gives the full circuit as roughly 12.6 km and 9 h.
caveat: Data thin — verify with the hut before going. Very much a wilderness day.

name: Greitspitz-Klettersteig
approach: 30 min from the Flimsattel lift station
lift: Samnaun cable cars to Alp Trida / Flimsattel
character: Built in 2001. A sports ferrata with two variants, one of them extremely exposed and graded K5, on the Silvretta border ridge.
caveat: Combines well with the easier Flimspitz route on the same lift ticket.

name: Flimspitz-Klettersteig
approach: From the Alp Trida / Flimsattel lift stations
character: Opened in 2004, with enjoyable slab climbing. The easier companion to the Greitspitz route next door.
caveat: The Samnaun lifts have limited summer operating dates — check before travelling.

name: Klettersteig La Resgia
approach: 15 min from the car park by the Seiler AG works yard, opposite Hotel Palü
character: Varied climbing with a wire bridge, mesh netting and ladders, and a choice of two difficulty levels partway. The slightly overhanging Adlerhorst crux makes you climb round an arête. Combine it with the Klettersteig Languard, which is more peaceful and leads to a very scenic top.
caveat: Starts straight from Pontresina, so no lift and no logistics — one of the most convenient routes in the Engadin. After the La Resgia exit, follow the signposted path towards Alp Languard for the second ferrata.

name: Klettersteig Piz Trovat (I & II)
grade: K2–K3; variant II up to K6
approach: 30 min from the Diavolezza top station
lift: Diavolezza cable car from the Bernina line station (15 min ride)
descent: 30 min back to the top station
descentFoot: ~1 h 30 down to the Bernina pass road
character: Steep entry ladder, then slabs, a rope bridge and an overhanging crux, with stupendous views over the Morteratsch and Pers glaciers. Piz Trovat II branches off and is savagely strenuous.
caveat: At 3146 m this is high — weather changes fast. The descent crosses scree and snow patches. Variant II needs Tyrolienne braking gear and real expertise.

name: Via ferrata du Tichodrome
approach: 30 min from Noiraigue station, or 5 min from the Restaurant du Haut de la Côte car park
descent: 30 min back to the station (or 5 min to the restaurant)
season: 15 July to 31 December (closed in spring for nesting birds)
character: Mostly a traverse across Jura limestone, well secured and generously equipped with holds, looking across the valley to the Creux du Van.
caveat: In the Jura rather than the Alps, but genuinely north of them. Closed for much of the first half of the year.
